Plus, the woman who lived with and loved Freddie Mercury as her fiance Martin Belam Tue 1 Sep 2026 06.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. A Las Vegas jury has found the former South Side Compton Crips gang leader Duane Keith Davis guilty of the murder of Tupac Shakur , bringing the case to a close nearly 30 years after the rapper was gunned down. The jury took about three hours to reach a guilty verdict in a case that relied heavily on multiple confessions from Davis himself. The 63-year-old, who was accused of instigating the deadly shooting but not pulling the trigger himself, had spent years telling investigators and interviewers alike of his direct involvement before he was arrested in 2023. Who was Tupac Shakur? Shakur was born in 1971 in East Harlem, New York, and rose to fame in the early 90s with lyrics that doubled as a sharp commentary on social injustice, including systemic racism and police brutality. He was 25 when he died and is regarded among the greatest rappers to ever live, and continues to be celebrated around the world years after his life was cut short. How have his family reacted to the trial? “We’ve been waiting 30 years to grieve properly,” Zayd Akinyela, Shakur’s cousin, told reporters outside the courtroom when the trial was under way. “A lot of people don’t get to grieve until they understand what happened to their loved one and how it happened.” Why have authorities been so heavily criticised over the case? Las Vegas police faced criticism that they had bungled the investigation and failed to pursue crucial leads, including from a member of Shakur’s entourage who claimed he could identify the shooters. That witness died weeks later in a separate shooting. Rescue attempts continue in areas devastated by flash floods in Nepal and Tibet with 1,000 dead View image in fullscreen A Nepali police helicopter carrying relief supplies lands in Rasuwa district. Photograph: Prabin Ranabhat/AFP/Getty Images The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris on Wednesday last week has risen to more than 1,000 . More than 4,400 are missing on the two sides of the border. Rescue efforts have been complicated by difficult terrain, persistently high flood waters and bad weather. With more than 40 bridges destroyed, rescuers are relying on helicopters, while India and China are sending prefabricated truss bridges to help restore access. The swollen Trishuli River has continued to change course unpredictably, making planning a challenge. Areas that were dry one day are flooded the next, and further floods are a constant concern. US army secretary Dan Driscoll resigns over reported friction with Pete Hegseth View image in fullscreen Dan Driscoll. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images The army secretary, Dan Driscoll, has handed his resignation to Donald Trump, the White House said Monday, becoming the latest high-profile figure to depart the defense department. The resignation comes after months of turmoil at the defense department, from leak investigations and budget issues to the ousting of several senior officials including the army chief of staff, Randy George, in April. In June, the army commander of forces in Europe and Africa, Gen Christopher Donahue, unexpectedly stepped down. What role had Driscoll been playing? An Iraq war veteran, tech investor and former adviser to JD Vance, Driscoll was tapped for the unusual role of key negotiator to try to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. He was also a major force behind trying to cut the red tape for military contractors to quickly develop more drones and counter-drone capabilities as warfare rapidly changes around the world. Teen charged with murder for recording San Diego mosque shooting live stream View image in fullscreen Candles with victims’ names written on them outside the Islamic Center of San Diego. Photograph: Ty ONeil/AP A 17-year-old North Carolina girl who recorded a live stream of a shooting that killed three people at a San Diego mosque and disseminated the attackers’ white-supremacist writings has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting , a district attorney said. The Forsyth county district attorney Jim O’Neill said the girl, whose name was not mentioned during the news conference, was arrested last week. On Monday a grand jury indicted her on three counts of murder and one count of conspiracy. Under North Carolina law, the aiding-and-abetting charges carry the same penalties as if the girl had committed the attack herself, O’Neill said. In other news … View image in fullscreen Donald Trump holds artists’ renderings of the White House plans. Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images A divided US supreme court has permitted Donald Trump to continue building his controversial $400m White House ballroom despite legal challenges, raising the likelihood it will be completed. New York City police shot and killed a woman after she stabbed two people , one of them fatally, in Times Square , an act authorities described as “random and unprovoked”. The US military has no plans to send troops to midterm polling sites, the highest‑ranking US military officer has said. US health officials have excluded two measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania from their counts . RFK Jr, the health secretary, has suggested the deaths were “fabricated” while the CDC said it was reviewing them. The Tennessee Volunteers will be honoring Dolly Parton with a helmet sticker this season , the college football team’s head coach, Josh Heupel, announced. Stat of the day: US trade regulator and 22 states accuse Amazon of taking $20bn with secret surcharges View image in fullscreen Amazon said it ‘strongly disagrees’ with the lawsuit. Photograph: Charles-McClintock Wilson/NurPhoto/Shutterstock The US’s main trade regulator and 22 states have sued Amazon , alleging the online retailer “secretly and systematically overcharged” advertisers, leading to higher costs for customers on items such as groceries and other essential goods. Amazon described it as a “misguided lawsuit” with which it “strongly disagrees”. Culture Pick: Ridiculed Olympic B-girl gets the last laugh … and it’s a total joy View image in fullscreen Raygun at the Paris Olympics. Photograph: Elsa/Getty Images She spent the biggest moment of her career at the Paris Olympics thrashing around like a toddler having a tantrum – then went viral globally. Now, a Netflix film reveals how the much-mocked breakdancer Raygun got over it. Don’t miss this: Mary Austin on her best friend and the love of her life, Freddie Mercury View image in fullscreen Freddie Mercury and Mary Austin circa 1977. Photograph: Courtesy of Mary Austin Freddie was loud, flamboyant, confident, supremely camp and gay. Mary was quiet, inhibited, diffident and strictly heterosexual. Simon Hattenstone speaks to the late Queen singer’s former fiance about their life together. … or this: Can we stop AI from deceiving us? View image in fullscreen Illustration: Alex Mellon/The Guardian We are used to the idea that our fellow humans may intentionally mislead or manipulate us, but the idea that machines can now do the same is deeply unsettling, as Snigdha Poonam’s long read explores . Climate check: How intense rains in the Grand Canyon turned into a deadly disaster View image in fullscreen Remnants of stone bridge pylons along Bright Angel Creek after a flash flood. Photograph: J Thompson/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images Scientists have long warned that the climate crisis will create stronger extremes and destructive shifts between wet and dry conditions, and the flash flooding in the Arizona tourist destination, which killed at least two people, was likely triggered by compounding climate factors such as local drought, recent wildfires and warming in the Pacific Ocean. Last Thing: Hiker, 91, becomes oldest person to complete grueling Appalachian Trail View image in fullscreen Dale Sanders. Photograph: Robert F Bukaty/AP Dale Sanders said he fell 71 times on the more than 2,000-mile Appalachian Trail but completed the journey as “people are motivated and given encouragement by my efforts”. Photograph: Dave Benett/Getty Images for Boodles Ellie Goulding Ellie Goulding admits error over promoting diamonds from controversial Australian mine Singer ‘mortified’ about wearing diamonds from Argyle mine at centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land Kevin Rawlinson Mon 19 Oct 2026 09.20 EDT Last modified on Mon 19 Oct 2026 09.21 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The singer Ellie Goulding has admitted her error at having promoted diamonds at the centre of environmental concerns about Indigenous land in Australia, despite having spent years campaigning on environmental issues – including the effects of mining on ancestral lands. She appeared at a event in London earlier this month for the jewellery brand Boodles, modelling some of its newly acquired pink diamonds , some of which came from a controversial mine in Western Australia. “Protecting the environment is a cause close to my heart. I always strive to uphold those values. Regretfully, in this instance, I fell short,” said Goulding, who was made an MBE for services to biodiversity and the climate last year. “I was not aware of the concerns surrounding the Argyle mine and I am grateful that it has been brought to my attention. “You will certainly not see me wearing diamonds originating from the Argyle mine again. The Indigenous and local communities affected deserve better. While I am mortified to have made this error in judgment, I am letting this moment serve as a reminder and an opportunity to continue to question the status quo, to learn and do better.” View image in fullscreen ‘You will certainly not see me wearing diamonds originating from the Argyle mine again,’ Goulding said. Photograph: Dave Benett/Getty Images for Boodles As well as serving as a global goodwill ambassador for the UN environment programme, Goulding is an ambassador for the environmental organisation WWF, which said it “takes seriously the environmental impact of mining and the effect it can have on Indigenous and local communities”. The charity added: “Ellie is a passionate advocate for nature and human rights and has championed the rights of Indigenous peoples as a WWF ambassador. We have discussed this issue with Ellie and continue to value her support.” A week before the Boodles event in London, it was announced the firm had bought the Argyle Pink Diamonds brand, as well as its inventory, from the mining firm Rio Tinto . A source close to Goulding suggested this timing may have led to the singer falling short of her own environmental values. View image in fullscreen The Argyle diamond mine in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. Mining ended there in 2020. Photograph: Murray Rayner/Nature Publishing Group/AFP/Getty Images According to the Daily Mirror, which first reported the news , the Gelganyem Group, which represents the traditional owners of the land that was mined for the diamonds, has expressed concerns about the state it has been left in by the industrial processes now the mining has ceased. The group told the paper: “Gelganyem chair Kia Dowell, a Gija woman, acknowledges Ellie Goulding’s apology and welcomes her recognition that Indigenous and local communities deserve better. She hopes it helps the public and Rio Tinto shareholders understand what is at stake at Argyle and the standard Rio Tinto’s mine closure must meet.” The paper quoted the organisation’s representative as saying traditional owners wanted “unrestricted access without unresolved risks being left for future generations”, adding that Pfas – or forever chemicals – were one of “several technical issues traditional owners, Gelganyem and independent experts have raised”. Rio Tinto said: “Mining at Argyle in Western Australia ended in 2020 after 37 years, and we are currently undertaking major mine closure works, including rehabilitation, with long-term monitoring and maintenance to follow. We acknowledge traditional owners as custodians of country. We are continuing to talk to them and their representatives, the Gelganyem Group, about closure, including Pfas.” Boodles has not responded to a request for comment. The Mirror quoted a source close to the firm as saying it was not responsible for the mine itself and adding: “Boodles have bought the last batch of pink diamonds and assets from Rio Tinto including their website and Instagram account.
